source.authors: Joyce P. S. Leung, Jenny S. Cory, J. Todd Kabaluk, Alida F. Janmaat
source.title: Effect of Collection Month, Visible Light, and Air Movement on the Attraction of Male Agriotes obscurus L. (Coleoptera: Elateridae) Click Beetles to Female Sex Pheromone

method: behavioural arena assay: single beetle in a Petri-dish arena with a cellulose granule impregnated (1% wt/wt) with a 1:1 synthetic blend of geranyl octanoate and geranyl hexanoate, or a blank granule; walking speed, distance and time moving scored
conditions: Field-collected males (wild, not lab-reared; pheromone-baited pitfall traps, Agassiz Research and Development Centre, British Columbia, 2014 and 2015; age unknown). Light experiment: white light (0.8 klux) against red light (0 lux, used as a proxy for darkness), crossed with pheromone against blank, 9 to 12 beetles per light x pheromone x collection-month combination over six days. Stimulus is a nominal loading (0.03 g of 1% granule in this trial); release rate was not measured. Nulls: the presence of visible light had no impact on any movement parameter and did not affect the response to pheromone; in this experiment April-collected beetles walked faster and farther than May-collected beetles (speed F1,67 = 6.24, p = 0.015; distance F1,67 = 5.62, p = 0.025) and May beetles spent 85.1% more time in the granule zone (F1,46 = 7.47, p = 0.009); in Experiment 1 (moving air) April beetles walked faster with pheromone but May beetles showed no pheromone effect (pheromone F1,63 = 0.00, p = 0.961), with collection month confounded with storage time; Experiment 3 found collection month affected activity but not the pheromone response. The same sentence also reports that pheromone beetles spent a greater proportion of time moving (F1,68 = 4.92, p = 0.030), cut from the quote. In the pheromone treatment 24% more beetles reached the granule zone (Wald chi2 = 8.98, p = 0.003) and those that reached it made 75.9% more contacts (F1,46 = 6.49, p = 0.014), but pheromone did not increase the duration of contact with the granule zone (F1,45 = 0.56, p = 0.457). Beetles were held at 10 C in darkness until testing and this experiment ran in August 2014 on April- and May-collected beetles, so storage lasted months; assay temperature and the order of treatments are not stated.
quote: As expected, beetles exposed to pheromone walked 72% faster and 31% farther than beetles in the blank control (speed: F1,67 = 27.0, p =< 0.001; distance: F1,67 = 28.52, p < 0.001) …
note: Sentence cut after the distance statistic (cut text: ', and also spent a greater proportion of time moving (F1,68 = 4.92, p = 0.030).'); the whole sentence is 47 words. The cut adds a third result and drops no qualifier of the quoted two. source.authors: Dae-Yun Kim, Theerachart Leepasert, Michael J. Bangs, Theeraphap Chareonviriyaphap
source.title: Dose–Response Assay for Synthetic Mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) Attractant Using a High-Throughput Screening System

method: dose-response attraction assay in a high-throughput screening system with a synthetic lure
conditions: Laboratory NIH strain (National Institute of Health, Thailand), colony maintained nearly 40 years, females 3 to 5 days old, nulliparous, mated; not wild-caught. High-Throughput Screening System (HITSS, three cylinders, 2.75 L, dark); BG-lure (lactic acid, ammonium hydrogen carbonate, hexanoic acid) at ten nominal doses from 10 g to 0.005 g; 20 females per replicate, 9 replicates per dose, 10 min; percent attraction = ((Nt - Nu)/(Nt + Nu)) x 100, 100 fully attracted, -100 fully repelled. Doses are nominal masses of lure, not measured emission. Overall mosquitoes were repelled from 1.0 g to 10.0 g (abstract). Positive control 1 g dry ice; the Methods list a no-lure negative control but report no result for it. Females were sugar-fed, then starved 12 h (water only) before testing; Culex was tested 18:00 to 24:00, Aedes 06:00 to 12:00. The index counts only females that entered a cylinder: at 0.025 g a mean 6.0 +/- 3.7 of 20 females were in the treated cylinder (Results), so most did not respond. The per-dose Table 1 (mean +/- SD) is an image and was not read; the order of doses is not stated. Culex: attraction began at 0.5 g (10.0%) and reached 75.9% at 0.005 g (Results 3.2.2); 10 g gave -50.2%; 1 g dry ice attracted 76.0% +/- 26.3%. The abstract gives no test statistic for the Culex optimum, and the Results give none separating 0.025 g (88.9%) from 0.005 g (75.9%); whether the abstract's 'without significant difference within species (p > 0.05)' covers Culex is not stated. Kruskal-Wallis across doses, Mann-Whitney within and between species.
quote: Cx. quinquefasciatus showed a greater positive percent attraction (88.9%) at 0.025 g, whereas the USDA and Pu Teuy Ae. aegypti produced optimum attractant activation at 0.005 g (72.6% and 58.9%, respectively) without significant difference within species (p > 0.05).
note: Quote is the whole abstract sentence (39 words); the Culex value is its first clause, the Aedes values in the rest are filed on the next line. Species named in the quote by abbreviation; Methods give Culex quinquefasciatus. Family Culicidae, order Diptera as on main for Aedes aegypti; GBIF ACCEPTED in gbif-names.tsv. Not on main under this DOI or species+sense_chemical. Licence: MDPI page CC BY 3.0; Crossref CC BY 4.0 content-version vor. Crossref authors, volume 12, issue 4 agree with page.

source.title: Dose–Response Assay for Synthetic Mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) Attractant Using a High-Throughput Screening System

method: dose-response attraction assay in a high-throughput screening system with a synthetic lure
conditions: Two strains: USDA, a permethrin-susceptible laboratory strain maintained over 50 years; Pu Teuy, a permethrin-resistant population collected as immatures from containers in Kanchanaburi Province, Thailand, January 2019, F2 to F3 generation females in the HITSS assay (F1 to F3 in the permethrin susceptibility assay). High-Throughput Screening System (HITSS, three cylinders, 2.75 L, dark); BG-lure (lactic acid, ammonium hydrogen carbonate, hexanoic acid) at ten nominal doses from 10 g to 0.005 g; 20 females per replicate, 9 replicates per dose, 10 min; percent attraction = ((Nt - Nu)/(Nt + Nu)) x 100, 100 fully attracted, -100 fully repelled. Doses are nominal masses of lure, not measured emission. Overall mosquitoes were repelled from 1.0 g to 10.0 g (abstract). Positive control 1 g dry ice; the Methods list a no-lure negative control but report no result for it. Females were sugar-fed, then starved 12 h (water only); Aedes was tested 06:00 to 12:00, Culex 18:00 to 24:00. The USDA series in the Results text is not monotonic and shows repellency below 1 g: 0.005 g 72.6%, 0.025 g 21.3%, 0.05 g 53.5%, 0.1 g -29.3%, 0.15 g 3.5%, 0.2 g -51.9%, 0.5 g -22.2%, 1.0 g -40.0%, 5.0 g -87.0%, 10 g -96.3%; for Pu Teuy the text gives only the 0.005 g value (Table 1 is an image, not read), and its response to dry ice is not reported. The order of doses is not stated. 10 g strongly repelled both strains (-96.3% susceptible, -100% resistant; no difference, p = 0.317); 0.05 g against 0.005 g in USDA was not significant (p = 0.287); Aedes USDA was attracted to 1 g dry ice at only 12.2%, significantly less than Culex (p = 0.002).
quote: Cx. quinquefasciatus showed a greater positive percent attraction (88.9%) at 0.025 g, whereas the USDA and Pu Teuy Ae. aegypti produced optimum attractant activation at 0.005 g (72.6% and 58.9%, respectively) without significant difference within species (p > 0.05).
note: Same whole abstract sentence as the Culex line; Aedes part is the second clause. Ae. aegypti is not defined in the quote by full name (Methods name the species). value: in neonates from non-crayfish-eating localities, ln tongue-flick attack score was 1.3 times (molted crayfish swab) and 1.2 times (unmolted) higher than for water control 0.69 +/- 0.33 (F2,99 = 3.28, P = 0.04)

source.authors: Javier Manjarrez, Constantino Macías Garcia, Hugh Drummond
source.title: Congenital feeding response to a novel prey in a Mexican gartersnake

method: behavioural: tongue-flick and strike scoring toward prey-scented swabs, naive laboratory-born neonates
conditions: Wild-caught gravid females were housed in the laboratory and their neonates, born in captivity, were tested at 14 days old. Underwater test with swabs saturated by 30 s immersion in water holding freshly molted or unmolted crayfish (1:1 volume), or distilled water as control, presented to each neonate in random order at 20 to 40 min intervals, up to 60 s each; tongue-flick attack score (TFAS), ln-transformed. NC (non-crayfish-eating) localities: 253 neonates from 34 clutches; C (crayfish-eating) localities: 65 neonates from 15 clutches (sample sizes of the chemosensory subset are smaller in the Results df). Swabs carry chemical cues only; no visual cue was part of the design. Population contrast: neonates from crayfish-eating (C) localities did not respond differently from control (F2,42 = 0.52, P = 0.60; filed as the next line); the relative response to control did not differ between populations (t47 = 0.53, P = 0.70). Attacks were rare: 11.5% of NC and 3.1% of C neonates attacked a swab; NC neonates attacked soft and hard crayfish swabs in similar percentages but did not attack control-water swabs, and attacks on soft crayfish swabs (N = 328) outnumbered those on hard (N = 151; G = 5.34, df = 1, P = 0.02) in both populations. Analysis: generalized linear mixed model (repeated-measures ANOVA) on ln-TFAS with sex and litter as random factors and population type as fixed factor; no pairwise test of each crayfish swab against water is reported in the text read. Neonates were unfed from birth (yolk reserve). Collected under SEMARNAT scientific collecting permit FAUT-0188.
quote: In the neonates from NC localities, ln-TFAS for soft crayfish … and hard crayfish … were 1.3 and 1.2 times higher, respectively, than for the control water (0.69 ± 0.33; F2,99 = 3.28, P = 0.04; Fig. 1).
note: Two cut marks stand for the means '(0.91 ± 0.36)' and '(0.88 ± 0.35)', which belong to the stimuli and drop no qualifier. 'Soft' is the freshly molted crayfish. Family Colubridae and order Squamata as on main for other Thamnophis rows (T. proximus, T. sirtalis); Thamnophis melanogaster is not a SYNONYM row in gbif-names.tsv. Held lead from the brief retried; no peerj.8718 hit on main or unit branches. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version unspecified. method: behavioural: tongue-flick and strike scoring toward prey-scented swabs, naive laboratory-born neonates
conditions: Wild-caught gravid females were housed in the laboratory and their neonates, born in captivity, were tested at 14 days old.
